target_customer: General public, journalists, researchers and policymakers (free); funded by donors and grants
problem: Reliable long-run data on global problems is scattered and hard to understand.
business_model: nonprofit funded by philanthropic grants and reader donations

founders.name: Max Roser
founders.background_notes: Social historian and development economist; began the project 2011, launched May 2013 (Wikipedia).

founders.name: Hannah Ritchie
founders.background_notes: Joined 2017, later Head of Research per Wikipedia; YC lists her as founder.

investors: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (via Oxford Martin School, 'almost 1.8M USD')
Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (general operating support)

technical_complexity.rationale: Data aggregation and interactive charts with open-source tooling; the hard part is curation, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Curated datasets, trust and reputation built since 2013; content is freely reusable under CC BY, so the moat is brand and curation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent attempted to absorb it in sources seen; Gapminder is a peer that OWID itself draws data from.

market_need_then: Demand shown by use: millions of monthly users and wide citation by media (YC page, company claim). No dated 2018-19 demand source collected.

identity.visual_style: Interactive charts released under CC BY with the logo on each chart.
identity.voice_and_tone: Educational, data-first, 'research and data to make progress against the world's largest problems'.

branding.brand_signature: Embeddable interactive charts carrying the OWID logo and CC BY stamp.
branding.community_and_virality: Won the 2019 Lovie Award (Wikipedia); widely cited in media; more than 4,000 reader donors.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised, award-winning web brand cited widely per Wikipedia and its own pages; the chart-with-logo reuse model spreads the brand. Breadth of media use not independently measured.

outcome_analysis: Our World in Data is a nonprofit that joined YC Winter 2019 as one of three nonprofits, so venture outcome metrics do not apply. It has been sustained by grants (Gates Foundation roughly 1.8M USD in 2018 and 1M USD in 2019, later Wellcome and others) and over 4,000 donors, with 2023 revenue of GBP 2.45M per Wikipedia. Success here means durable funding and reach; it declined a 7.5M USD FTX Future Fund offer in 2022 after due diligence, avoiding the later collapse.
notes: Nonprofit, not a venture comp; founded 2013 before the 2019 YC batch. The earlier record listed a 2022 USD 7.5M FTX Future Fund round; removed because Bloomberg quotes an OWID spokesperson saying it did due diligence and chose not to move forward (the grant was offered, not received; BBC via LongtermWiki claims a funding loss, which conflicts). Gates figures: Oxford Martin announcement 'almost 1.8M' (2018, via Oxford) and InfluenceWatch 1M general operating grant Sep 2019; InfluenceWatch is secondary. The funding page names Wellcome, Gates, Skip Foundation, Coefficient Giving, Mohn Westlake, with past grants from Quadrature Climate Foundation, YC and GiveWell, but no amounts; the Trustees' report has them. Revenue GBP 2.45M (2023) and 1.78M (2022) are from Wikipedia snapshots and conflict slightly in timing. No dated near-2019 competitor source found (Gapminder results undated), so the list is empty.
